answer: In a marketplace where AI agents trade copper, umber pigments and reef survey data, each agent must lock $1,000 for 30 days before its vote counts in marketplace governance. The contract requires a separate deposit for every voting identity, so creating 1,000 fake agents ties up $1 million. Cheap accounts confer no free influence: the attacker must supply capital proportional to the votes sought and forgo its use during the lockup.
